title: Senior's toolkit: EF Core in a web API
summary: The dotnet ef commands for shipping migrations, and the DbContext options and query methods for seeing and controlling what EF sends.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: EF Core in a web API
steps.body: What an experienced .NET engineer reaches for when a migration has to ship, a page is slow, or a save fails in production.

toolkit.what: Generate a migration from model changes. Read the generated code before committing: renames can come out as drop and add.
flags: the project with the DbContext / the one that runs (when they differ)
which context, when there are several
toolkit.example: dotnet ef migrations add AddSeatMap -o Data/Migrations --project src/Tickets.Data --startup-project src/Tickets.Api

toolkit.what: One SQL script that applies whatever is missing, whatever migration the target database is at. The release artifact a reviewer or DBA can read.
flags: guard each migration with a check of __EFMigrationsHistory
only the migrations between two names

toolkit.what: Build an executable that applies pending migrations, for deploy pipelines that should not need the .NET SDK or the source.
toolkit.example: dotnet ef migrations bundle --self-contained -r linux-x64 --output artifacts/efbundle

toolkit.what: Exit with an error when the model has changes no migration covers. Put it in CI so a forgotten migration fails the pull request, not the deploy.
flags: non-zero exit code when changes are pending

toolkit.what: Move a development database to exactly that migration, up or down. `0` removes every migration.
Print every SQL command with its duration. In ASP.NET Core, set the `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` log category to Information instead.
flags: better errors for bad data in columns
one query's SQL, without running it

toolkit.what: Prefix the SQL with a comment, so the query can be traced from pg_stat_statements, Query Store or a slow-query log back to the endpoint.
flags: add the file and line of the call (EF Core 7+)

toolkit.what: SQL Server (and Npgsql): retry commands that fail with transient errors, such as a failover or a dropped connection. With it, wrap your own transactions in `db.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync(...)`.

steps.prompt: The deploy job must bring staging (two migrations behind) and production (five behind) up to date with the same artifact, and the DBA wants to read it first. What does the release build produce?
options: `dotnet ef database update` run from the build agent
`dotnet ef migrations script` with no options
Nothing: the app calls `Database.Migrate()` on start-up
steps.explain: A plain script assumes an empty database. `database update` needs the SDK, the source and the production connection string on the build agent. The idempotent script is one readable file that works on both.

steps.prompt: Make CI fail a pull request that changes the model without a migration.
Match the symptom to the tool that shows you the cause.
pairs: The DBA sees a slow query and asks which endpoint sends it
A page is slow and you suspect N+1
command logging with `LogTo` or the Database.Command log category
You want the SQL of one LINQ query in a unit test
A save fails with "expected to affect 1 row(s), but actually affected 0"
Occasional failures during a SQL Server failover

steps.prompt: You renamed a property. Put the steps to ship it safely in order.
lines: Read the migration and replace any DropColumn/AddColumn pair with RenameColumn
Commit; CI runs has-pending-model-changes and the tests
The release build runs dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent
The deploy applies the script, then rolls out the app

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Every EF call in a request is async and takes `ct`; reads are `AsNoTracking()` or projections; hot queries carry a `TagWith`; concurrency failures become 409s; and schema changes ship as reviewed, idempotent scripts or bundles, never as `EnsureCreated()` or a surprise `Migrate()` at start-up.
